standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels definition-bivariant-class (proof lines 6762 and 6782) and lemma-base-change-envelope (proof line 6766); definition-envelope (proof line 6710)
standard_prerequisites.use: Fix the three conditions that the descended operation must satisfy and guarantee that the base change Y'_1 -> Y_1 of an envelope is again an envelope, so the same lift can be performed after any locally finite type base change.

core_obligations: Build the candidate operation: for beta in CH_k(Y) choose a lift beta' in CH_k(Y') using exactness for the envelope g, and set c cap beta = h_*(c' cap beta') (proof lines 6732-6741).

Show the definition is independent of the lift: for gamma in CH_k(Y' times_Y Y') the difference of two lifts is p_* gamma - q_* gamma, and the bivariant class axiom plus h o a = h o b gives h_*(c' cap (p_* gamma - q_* gamma)) = h_*(a_*(c' cap gamma) - b_*(c' cap gamma)) = 0 (proof lines 6742-6752); note also that the choice is forced by res(c) = c' (proof lines 6754-6757).

Extend the construction to every base change Y_1 -> Y locally of finite type, where Y'_1 -> Y_1 is an envelope by base change, and verify the conditions of the bivariant class definition: condition (1) for a proper t : Y_2 -> Y_1 is checked by transporting a lift beta'_2 along t' and using the cartesianness of the two squares, and conditions (2) and (3) are said by the author to be proved in the same manner (proof lines 6760-6822).
proof_roadmap: Define c cap beta by lifting beta along the envelope and pushing forward c' cap beta' (proof lines 6732-6741).
Prove well-definedness from the exact sequence of the envelope and the bivariant axiom (proof lines 6742-6757).
Base change the whole diagram, repeat the construction, and check the bivariant class conditions, condition (1) in detail and the rest by the same argument (proof lines 6760-6822).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a descent statement for bivariant classes: given c' on X' -> Y' over an envelope Y' -> Y whose two restrictions to X' times_X X' coincide, one must produce a unique c on X -> Y restricting to c' (statement lines 6706-6718, tag 0GUC). The proof has to construct the operation itself, first on CH_k(Y) by lifting along the envelope and pushing forward, then on every locally finite type base change, and it must verify the well-definedness through the exact sequence for envelopes and the bivariant axiom h_* a_* = h_* b_*. Condition (1) of the bivariant definition is checked in full by transporting lifts along a proper morphism; the author states that the remaining two conditions are proved in the same manner and omits the details, so the claim is H2.
